answer: Random-walk audit over the interaction grove: each epoch a public beacon samples one vertex, and that identity must open its full interaction history for peer replay. A failed replay burns the ember escrowed at registration and slashes every neighbor that attested it. A clone farm shares a single history root, so one sampled vertex exposes the whole cluster: expected loss scales with cluster size N, not with per-head fees, so a sybil majority costs quadratically while an honest pair pays only its own stake.
